newsitem.title: THAILAND: Favoured Thai stocks hit limit, sales after poll.
newsitem.headline: Favoured Thai stocks hit limit, sales after poll.

text.p: Heavy selling of large capitalised stocks by retail and foreign investors on negative election news sent many favoured Thai shares down their 10 percent limit in the morning market session on Monday.
Among finance stocks down the limit were Dhana Siam Finance and Securities, dowm 8.50 baht to 80, Finance One down 7.5 to 68.5, National Finance and Securities off 6.5 to 61.
Banks were also heavily sold. Siam City Bank was down 3.5 to 32, state-owned Krung Thai Bank fell eight baht to 76.5 and Thai Military Bank was off 6.5 to 67.5.
Only Bangkok Bank, down 13 to 199 and Siam Commercial Bank off 16 to 202 showed any real resistance, brokers said.

Communications stocks, heavily favoured last week, were also down sharply. Much traded TelecomAsia was down 4.50 to 55.5. Thai Telephone and Telecommunication was down the limit losing 04.75 to 43.75.
Thai stocks were down 56.83 points or 5.68 percent to 943.90 by the lunch break as investors viewed neop, head of research at Crosby Securities.
"The market says it all. Buying in the last two weeks was on the expectation of a positive election outcome now it seems like nothing has really changed," she said.
Chavalit is aiming to form a coalition with four parties who were his partners in the controversial outgoing administration of premier Banharn Silpa-archa.
Across the board, only 10 issues advanced, 11 were unchanged and 304 declined.
